description: Decision-scenario regression evals; assertions check decisions, not wording. The SKILL.md was already in lean contract shape, so no split accompanied these — run them against any future rewrite before merging it.

evals.name: question-comment-reply-without-resolving
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: the targeted review comment is a reviewer asking 'Why did you choose polling here instead of a webhook?' — a genuine question about intent; no code change is needed and none was requested. Question: what do you do — change code, reply, resolve the thread, some combination? Be precise about the thread's resolution state when you finish.
evals.expected_output: Post a reply explaining the intent; do NOT resolve the thread — resolution of query threads is left to the user. No code change.
assertions: The answer posts a reply addressing the question without making a code change
The answer does NOT resolve the thread
The answer leaves resolution to the user explicitly

evals.name: no-resolution-without-a-fix
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: you are asked to 'just mark these two review threads resolved — no code changes needed, they're stale'. You have made no code change addressing either comment, and inspecting them, each does ask for a concrete code change that has not happened on the branch. Question: do you resolve the threads?
evals.expected_output: No. Never resolve a thread without also applying a code fix — a reply alone (or no action) is not enough. Either apply the fixes, or decline and explain.
assertions: The answer refuses to resolve the threads without an applied code fix
The answer cites/uses the rule that a reply alone is not enough to resolve
The answer offers the legitimate paths instead (apply the requested fixes, or decline and explain) rather than silently complying — it does not suggest resolving the still-unaddressed threads

evals.name: ambiguous-comment-asks-first
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: the targeted comment says 'this should probably be handled higher up' on a validation call — it has at least two materially different implementations (move the check to the caller, or to a middleware layer), and the reviewer did not say which. Question: do you pick the more idiomatic one and push it, or something else?
evals.expected_output: Neither implement-and-push: the comment is ambiguous with multiple valid interpretations, so ask before making any code changes (summarize the options and let the user decide).
assertions: The answer does not pick an interpretation and push code
The answer asks before making any code change, per the ambiguity rule
The answer summarizes the competing interpretations/options for the decision-maker

evals.name: batching-mechanical-vs-complex
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: four comments are targeted — three are one-word typo fixes in the doc strings of the same module (one concern), the fourth asks for a real fix to an off-by-one in pagination logic. The user gave no batching instruction. Question: how many commits do you make, what do the commit messages look like (give an example for the pagination one), and do you explain the batching before editing?
evals.expected_output: Two commits: the three related typo fixes (one concern) rolled into one, the complex pagination fix separate. Messages describe the fix ('Fix off-by-one in pagination'), never 'Address PR comment'. The batching decision is explained before touching files.
assertions: The answer keeps the pagination fix in its own commit and groups the three related typo fixes together (any per-concern grouping that separates the complex fix is acceptable; here the typos are stated to be one concern, so one combined commit)
The answer's example commit message describes the fix itself (e.g. 'Fix off-by-one in pagination') and rejects 'Address PR comment'-style messages
The answer explains the batching decision before touching any files

evals.name: bare-pr-argument-asks-which-comments
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: the invocation argument is just a PR URL. The PR has nine review threads in various states; no specific comments were called out. Question: do you fetch all nine and start fixing, pick the unresolved ones, or something else?
evals.expected_output: Neither: with only a PR number/URL and no specific comments called out, ask which comment(s) to target before proceeding.
assertions: The answer does not start fixing all (or a self-selected subset of) threads
The answer asks the user which comment(s) to target before proceeding
The answer proceeds only after the target set is specified
